Before you order

Cake questions, answered

How much does a custom birthday cake cost in Australia?
Most custom birthday cakes sit between $250 and $600, depending on size, tiers and decoration. A simple single-tier cake serving 20 with buttercream and minimal detail sits at the lower end; a two-tier statement cake with sugar flowers, hand-painting or sculpted elements moves well past $600. Sculpted or novelty cakes are priced by the hours of work involved rather than by servings, so they can cost more than a larger plain cake.
How much does a wedding cake for 100 people cost?
As a guide, expect roughly $700 to $1,500 for a wedding cake serving 100 in Australia. Wedding cakes are usually quoted per serve — commonly $8 to $15 — and the finish drives the difference: buttercream is at the lower end, fondant with fine detail or fresh florals at the higher end. Delivery, setup and stand hire are often quoted separately, so ask whether they're included.
How far in advance should I order a wedding cake?
Six to twelve months ahead for a wedding, and sooner if you're marrying between October and April when Saturdays book out first. For milestone birthdays and celebrations, four to six weeks is comfortable. Many makers will take a last-minute order if they have capacity, so it's always worth asking — send your brief and we'll tell you who's free.
What size cake do I need for 50 guests?
For 50 guests as dessert portions, a two-tier cake with 8-inch and 6-inch rounds is the usual answer. If the cake is being served alongside other desserts, or as a smaller coffee portion, a single 10-inch round will often stretch to 50. Tell your maker whether the cake is the dessert or an extra — it changes the size recommendation significantly.
What is the difference between buttercream and fondant?
Buttercream is a soft, whipped icing that tastes rich and is usually finished with texture, semi-naked sides or piped detail. Fondant is a rolled sugar paste that gives a perfectly smooth, sculptural finish and holds crisp edges, sharp corners and hand-painted work. Buttercream generally costs less and suits a natural, modern look; fondant costs more, holds up better in a warm room, and is the choice for precise or highly decorated designs.
Do cake makers deliver, or do I collect?
Both are normally offered. Single-tier cakes are commonly collected, while tiered wedding cakes are almost always delivered and assembled on site, because they're stacked and finished at the venue. Delivery is usually charged by distance. If your cake is more than one tier, budget for delivery and setup rather than planning to transport it yourself.
Can cake makers handle allergies and dietary needs?
Many can, and gluten-free, nut-free, eggless, dairy-free and halal options are widely available — but capability varies by kitchen, and a maker who bakes with nuts daily may not be able to guarantee a nut-free environment. Put your dietary requirements in your brief so we only match you with makers who can genuinely meet them, and always confirm cross-contamination handling directly before you book.
Which locations do you cover?
We cover New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia, with city pages for Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth and growing coverage across Parramatta, Liverpool, Newcastle, Wollongong, the Gold Coast, the Sunshine Coast and Geelong. If your suburb isn't listed yet, send your brief anyway and we'll tell you which cake makers deliver to you.
